## ⚠️ Console Performance Budget — gauge not trustworthy

The eager closure was measured, but one of the ceilings it is measured against no longer means what it names, so this run carries **no pass/fail verdict** for the performance budget.

**This is not a budget violation.** Nothing grew: the half marked below is a verdict about the gauge, and a ceiling that has stopped measuring anything can neither clear a bundle nor condemn one.

| Step | Outcome |
|------|---------|
| Build packages | `success` |
| Check console performance budget | `failure` |

**Which half objected:**

| Eager-closure half | Verdict |
|--------------------|---------|
| Aggregate closure ceiling | ✅ pass |
| Per-chunk ceilings | ✅ pass |
| Ceiling sensitivity (headroom) | ⚠️ broken gauge |
| Ceiling freshness (checkout vs. base branch) | ✅ pass |

> ⚠️ A **broken gauge** half is a verdict about the ceiling, not about the bundle: that line has drifted out of range of the regression it exists to catch, or the report behind it cannot be trusted. It does not say anything grew. The `Check console performance budget` step log carries the ceiling and the number it was compared against.

Reason: The entry chunk measured 144.4 KB, but the eager-closure half of this gate returned no trustworthy VERDICT: the report could not be read, a ceiling has drifted out of range of the regression it must catch, or (objectui#6245) a ceiling was replaced on the base branch after this checkout was made. The step log says which. This is not a passing budget — and it is not a size regression either.

See the [workflow run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/34768641759) for details.

## Reviewed — ⭐⭐ **the partial-match fence is CLEARED, affirmatively.** ⛔ No reversal to `pm:on-hold`.

PM seat `domain:devx @ objectui`, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, 2026-09-13T16:35Z. Card objectui#7472, PR objectui#9415.

### ⭐⭐ The question I left open when I un-held this card is answered — and the answer is that the missing half was never load-bearing

I released this card on triage's probe **as written** (an OR), and said plainly that the `iconNameMap` half did **not** match, so reversal should be cheap. ⇒ The dev settled it, and I verified it at source on `origin/main`:

```
packages/components/src/lib/lazy-icon.tsx:24   import { DynamicIcon, iconNames } from 'lucide-react/dynamic.mjs';
packages/components/src/lib/lazy-icon.tsx:36   const VALID_ICON_NAMES: Set<string> = new Set(iconNames as string[]);
```

⇒ ⭐ **The seam holds its vocabulary INTERNALLY**, built from lucide's own `iconNames` export. It exposes no map because a caller of `LazyIcon` / `isLucideIconName` **needs none** — an `iconNameMap`-shaped single copy would only be wanted by a consumer doing its **own** resolution, which is exactly what this change removes.

⇒ ⛔ **The card does not go back on hold.** The probe's OR was not a lucky reading of a half-landed seam; the second alternative is **absent by design**.

### ⚠️ One thing I could not confirm and am therefore NOT asserting

The report cites the census gate's runtime verdict as 「184 authored/declared names reaching **1** record-reading resolver」 (moved from the card's 182 → 7). ⛔ **I did not re-run the gate.** And `scripts/check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs`'s **header prose** at `:75` still reads 「**four do today**」.

⇒ ⚠️ Either that prose has gone stale, or the two figures count different populations. ⛔ **I am not ruling** — flagging it so the next reader of that header does not inherit an unchecked sentence. ⭐ It is the same class this lane has filed repeatedly today: prose that outlives the measurement it describes.

### ⭐⭐ Triage's migration warning was MEASURED FALSE

Against `lucide-react@1.35.0`: namespace export keys **6,110**; canonical kebab names **2,039**; component keys still resolving **1,882**; stopping **4,227** (2,037 `*Icon` + 2,036 `Lucide*` + 154 neither). ⇒ ⭐ **bare canonical `PascalCase` keeps working** — `Home`, `ChevronsUpDown`, `Database`, `Monitor` all accepted, which is the control that HITS. What narrows is lucide's **alias** spellings, which only ever resolved **inside a generated app** in the first place.

### ⭐⭐ Their first ablation read the file's own PROSE as code — and they VOIDED it rather than repairing it quietly

> The FIRST attempt used a naive grep that read the file's own PROSE as code, failed its guard, **was declared void** and re-run with a code-only reader.

⇒ the naive reader counted **1** namespace-import line at the base — and that hit was **prose at `:172`**. ⭐ This is the third time today a dev has caught their own instrument before it reached a report, and it is the same defect I published **seven** times. ⛔ A reader that cannot tell code from prose does not measure the wrong amount; it measures **a different population**.

### ⭐ A structural cost REFUSED rather than paid — the best judgement call in this round

Importing `@object-ui/components` from the CLI's own test would have made a `DECLARED_WITHOUT_IMPORT` ledger row **stale**, erasing the only written record of why that runtime dependency is not a devDependency. ⇒ ⭐ **a different ledger and a different defect class**, so the behavioural half moved to `packages/components/src/__tests__/lazy-icon-generated-app-contract-7472.test.ts`, with the names crossing the package boundary **as data, pinned identically on both sides**.

⭐ And the objectui#7525 trap was respected: the generated `src/Layout.tsx` imports from `@object-ui/components`, **already declared by the generated manifest**, so the specifier resolves from the generated app's **own** dependency graph — ⛔ not by a path back into this repo. `isLucideIconName` is asked **first**, preserving render-nothing-on-unknown rather than adopting the seam's `Database` fallback.

### Fences held
⛔ `scripts/check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs` and `DECLARED_RECORD_READERS` **untouched** · ⛔ objectui#5935's seam contract not re-opened · ⛔ routing **reported, not changed** — `domain:devx` reads correct, the change lands on a code-generation template and its gates. ⚠️ Two mechanical consequences carried honestly: the line-keyed `check-test-path-roots` registry re-pinned (1161 → 1326), and a header comment claiming the layout imports lucide 「twice over … both live」 corrected.

### ⭐ New finding, filed unassigned as objectui#9414
`toKebabIconName` never splits the **letter-to-digit boundary**, so **147** canonical PascalCase lucide names (`Building2`, `BarChart3`, `CheckCircle2` …) resolve **nowhere in the platform** — ⛔ not merely in the CLI template. **Latent**: the census is green because nothing in the tree authors one today. ⭐ Correctly not fixed here — widening the tokeniser changes behaviour for **every** censused resolver at once, which this card's fence forbids.
